desc:
Return all integers that have exactly n digits (no leading zero) and in which the absolute difference between every two neighbouring digits is exactly k. The numbers may be returned in any order, each one only once.

Example: n = 3, k = 7 gives 181, 292, 707, 818, 929. Note that 070 does not count because it starts with a zero.
hints: There are at most 9 * 10<sup>n-1</sup> candidates, far too many to test one by one for n = 9. Build the numbers digit by digit instead.
Given the last digit d, the next digit must be d + k or d - k, if that is a digit between 0 and 9.
Start the search from every first digit 1..9. When k = 0 the two options d + k and d - k are the same digit, so make sure the number is not produced twice.
editorial: Run a depth-first search that extends a partial number by one digit at a time. From last digit d the only possible next digits are d + k and d - k. Skip candidates outside 0..9, and when k = 0 try just one of them, otherwise the same number would be reported twice.

Every first digit 1..9 starts a binary tree of depth n - 1, so there are at most 9 * 2n-1 numbers (2,304 for n = 9) and the search visits no dead branches other than the digit-range cut-offs. Carrying the number as an integer (value * 10 + digit) avoids building strings.
